title: Adversarial neutralization: can a benign-looking prompt prefix cancel a steering vector?

original_idea.body: Adversarial neutralization: black-box prompt search for benign-looking prefixes that cancel a steering vector. Open model, single GPU.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: demonstrating steering can be silently neutralized bears directly on whether steering is a robust guardrail (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Black-box prompt search, no gradients; mentor-guided novice feasible though search design needs care (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable (neutralizing-prefix demonstration), search loop adds modest complexity (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly threat-model work on open models, addresses an explicit open problem (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only black-box search on single GPU (level 4).

novelty.reasoning: Targets a stated open problem; black-box neutralization of steering may be mostly unstudied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Explicit open problem; black-box prompt neutralization of steering appears underexplored.
